say.en: Every grain of rice you eat began as carbon dioxide in the air. Melvin Calvin used radioactive carbon to trace exactly how a leaf builds sugar from it. In this lesson: Identify the primary CO 2 acceptor and the first stable product in C 3 plants.
Describe carboxylation, reduction and regeneration.
Calculate ATP and NADPH needed per CO 2 and per glucose.

body.en: ATP and NADPH from the light reaction are used in the stroma to fix CO₂ into carbohydrate. Using radioactive ¹⁴C in algae, Melvin Calvin found that the first CO₂ fixation product is a 3-carbon organic acid, 3-phosphoglyceric acid (PGA); plants in which this happens are C₃ plants. The primary CO₂ acceptor is the 5-carbon ketose sugar ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP). The cycle has three stages. *Carboxylation*: CO₂ is fixed to RuBP by the enzyme RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase (RuBisCO), giving two molecules of 3-PGA; this is the most crucial step. Reduction: using 2 ATP and 2 NADPH per CO₂ fixed, PGA is reduced to triose phosphate, and glucose is formed. Regeneration: RuBP is regenerated so the cycle continues, using 1 ATP per CO₂.

points.en: Primary acceptor: RuBP (5C); first stable product: 3-PGA (3C).

say.en: ATP and NADPH from the light reaction are used in the stroma to fix CO 2 into carbohydrate. Using radioactive to the power 14C in algae, Melvin Calvin found that the first CO 2 fixation product is a 3-carbon organic acid, 3-phosphoglyceric acid PGA; plants in which this happens are C 3 plants. The primary CO 2 acceptor is the 5-carbon ketose sugar ribulose bisphosphate RuBP. The cycle has three stages. Carboxylation: CO 2 is fixed to RuBP by the enzyme RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase RuBisCO, giving two molecules of 3-PGA; this is the most crucial step. Reduction: using 2 ATP and 2 NADPH per CO 2 fixed, PGA is reduced to triose phosphate, and glucose is formed. Regeneration: RuBP is regenerated so the cycle continues, using 1 ATP per CO 2. Primary acceptor: RuBP 5C; first stable product: 3-PGA 3C.

say.en: RuBisCO catalyses carboxylation.
Per CO 2: 3 ATP plus 2 NADPH.

narration.en: Let us draw the three stages of the Calvin cycle and count the cost of one glucose.

say.en: Carboxylation: RuBisCO fixes CO₂ onto RuBP, a 5-carbon sugar. The unstable product splits into two molecules of 3-PGA.
Reduction: ATP and NADPH from the light reaction turn 3-PGA into triose phosphate, the stuff of sugars.
Regeneration: one more ATP rebuilds the CO₂ acceptor RuBP, so the cycle can go on.
So each CO₂ fixed costs 3 ATP and 2 NADPH.
One glucose has six carbons, so the cycle turns six times: 6 CO₂, 18 ATP and 12 NADPH go in.
Let us draw the three stages of the Calvin cycle and count the cost of one glucose.

caption.en: Each turn fixes one CO2. Carboxylation: RuBisCO joins CO2 to RuBP, giving two 3-PGA. Reduction: 2 ATP and 2 NADPH turn them into sugar phosphate. Regeneration: 1 more ATP remakes RuBP. So each CO2 costs 3 ATP and 2 NADPH, and six turns make one glucose (18 ATP, 12 NADPH).
caption.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಸುತ್ತು ಒಂದು CO2 ಸ್ಥಿರೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: ಕಾರ್ಬಾಕ್ಸಿಲೀಕರಣ, ಅಪಕರ್ಷಣ (2 ATP, 2 NADPH), ಪುನರ್ನಿರ್ಮಾಣ (1 ATP). ಪ್ರತಿ CO2 ಗೆ 3 ATP, 2 NADPH; ಆರು ಸುತ್ತು ಒಂದು ಗ್ಲೂಕೋಸ್ (18 ATP, 12 NADPH).

title.en: Counting the cost of one glucose

body.en: One *glucose* has six carbons, so six CO₂ must be fixed and the cycle must turn six times. Each turn uses 3 ATP and 2 NADPH, so one glucose needs 18 ATP and 12 NADPH. The cyclic flow of electrons helps meet the extra ATP demand, since non-cyclic flow alone gives ATP and NADPH in roughly equal amounts.

say.en: Let us work through this together. How many ATP and NADPH molecules are needed to make 3 molecules of glucose by the Calvin cycle? How many turns of the cycle does this take?
One glucose needs 6 CO 2, i.e. 6 turns, 18 ATP and 12 NADPH.
3 glucose need 3 times 6 equals 18 turns.
ATP equals 3 times 18 equals 54; NADPH equals 3 times 12 equals 36.
So the answer is 18 turns; 54 ATP and 36 NADPH.

body.en: For every CO₂ fixed: 3 ATP (2 for reduction + 1 for regeneration) and 2 NADPH. Multiply by 6 for glucose: 18 and 12.
